story.title: Russian Drone Attack Targets Ukraine's Security Service Headquarters in Kyiv
story.summary: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in central Kyiv on Friday afternoon, injuring five people, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The attack is seen as a significant escalation, with Zelensky accusing Moscow of targeting the personal office of the SBU head. He has instructed the SBU to respond appropriately to the strike.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the second-phase roadmap announced in late July 2026 for implementing President Trump’s broader Gaza peace framework. It links the decommissioning of Hamas and other armed groups’ weapons, a transition to Palestinian civilian administration, deployment of an international stabilization force, phased Israeli withdrawal, and Gaza’s reconstruction; implementation depends on agreed sequencing and verification.

facts.label: Announcement and framework
facts.value: The roadmap was made public on July 31, 2026, as “A Roadmap for Completing the Implementation of President Trump’s Comprehensive Peace Plan in Gaza,” and identifies the Comprehensive Plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025) as its international framework.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The plan concerns the Gaza Strip, with provisions addressing its governance, internal security, humanitarian assistance, reconstruction, armed groups, and the withdrawal of Israeli forces.

facts.label: Governance transition
facts.value: The roadmap calls for civilian governance and security functions to pass to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), while Resolution 2803 establishes the Board of Peace as the transitional body to coordinate the framework and redevelopment of Gaza.

facts.label: Security force and Israeli withdrawal
facts.value: A temporary International Stabilization Force is envisaged to monitor the ceasefire, support aid delivery, train Palestinian police, and support the transition. Israeli withdrawal is phased and linked to the disarmament process and an agreed timetable; Resolution 2803 authorizes the Board of Peace and related international presences through December 31, 2027, unless the Security Council acts further.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the roadmap’s announcement, responses, and related regional military tensions; it does not constitute a complete record of the Gaza war, prior ceasefire diplomacy, or all implementation activity.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the SBU headquarters a significant target?
explore_lenses.title: The strike hit an agency central to Ukraine's long-range campaign
explore_lenses.summary: The SBU is a domestic security agency but also a major actor in Ukraine's operations against Russian military and energy targets. Hitting its headquarters therefore carries operational and symbolic significance beyond another strike on Kyiv.

claims.text: Reuters described the SBU as central to Ukraine's war effort because it conducts deep strikes against Russia's military-industrial capacity and energy infrastructure.
Reuters reported that Ukrainian government buildings have rarely been damaged in Russian drone and missile strikes during the full-scale war, making this attack unusual in that respect.

Zelenskyy's assertion that the drone was aimed at Poklad's office is Ukraine's assessment of the intended target; the consulted reports did not provide an independent Russian confirmation of that intent.

story_report.summary: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service, or SBU, in central Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Initial reporting cited five people injured, though subsequent reports gave higher, differing casualty figures. Zelenskyy said the drone was directed at the office of acting SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad and ordered the agency to prepare a tangible response, with military support where needed.

sections.heading: Fire reported at SBU headquarters
sections.body: Ukrainska Pravda reported that Poklad was not in his office when the strike occurred and that it caused a fire in the building. Zelenskyy’s description of the intended target is Ukraine’s assessment; consulted reporting did not include independent Russian confirmation of the drone’s intended destination.

sections.heading: SBU role makes strike unusual
sections.body: Reuters described the SBU as a central part of Ukraine’s war effort, including through deep strikes on Russia’s military-industrial capacity and energy infrastructure. It also reported that Russian drone and missile attacks have rarely damaged Ukrainian government buildings during the full-scale war, making the reported hit on the SBU headquarters unusual in that respect.

sections.heading: Ukraine orders response as diplomacy remains uncertain
sections.body: Zelenskyy said he instructed Poklad to prepare an appropriate response that would, where possible, mirror the strike, with Ukrainian military support. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attack a major escalation and said it demonstrated Moscow’s rejection of diplomacy. Separately, a U.S. official told AP that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were expected to visit Moscow and Kyiv, but no schedule was publicly fixed and the Kremlin declined to confirm the trip.
